correctness.rationale: For any characteristic-p field, Frobenius makes every augmentation-ideal element p-nilpotent, so endomorphisms correspond to arbitrary generator tuples in that ideal. The invertible-cotangent condition characterizes automorphisms. For an idempotent map, lifts of an image basis and kernel basis yield an automorphism conjugating the map to a unique coordinate projection. Distinct image embeddings are counted by ordered independent cotangent vectors with arbitrary higher coefficients, divided by the exact automorphism-group size of the smaller truncated algebra. A fixed embedded image has exactly q^((m-r)(p^r-1)) right splittings because each omitted generator maps independently to its radical. Gaussian degrees give the sharp m=p+3 adjacent-rank reversal. Exhaustive tests at F2,m=2,3 yield rank counts (1,12,1) and (1,448,3584,1); F3,m=2 gives 5832 embeddings and 972 rank-one images. General statements rest on the proof, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Elementary abelian modular group algebras are central finite-dimensional objects in modular representation theory. Classification of all their algebra retractions and counting embedded images and splitting fibers are natural intrinsic endomorphism invariants over every finite field. The full rank census and the sharp asymptotic reversal of the two highest proper ranks at m=p+3 provide structural information not available from the basic flatness criterion; this is not a numerical one-off.
